title: First-Generation iStent Bypass Implantation versus ab Externo Canaloplasty Combined with Phacoemulsification in Patients with Primary Open Angle Glaucoma—12-Month Follow-Up

indication: mild-to-moderate primary open-angle glaucoma with visually significant cataract, target IOP not reached on maximum tolerated medication; no previous glaucoma surgery (prospective, non-randomized, single surgeon)

groups.description: phacoemulsification combined with first-generation iStent trabecular micro-bypass implantation (ab interno, inferonasal quadrant); one eye per patient
phacoemulsification combined with 360-degree ab externo canaloplasty (microcatheter and tensioning suture under two scleral flaps); one eye per patient

notes: Reference: Discussion states patients had no washout before surgery and baseline IOP was at maximum tolerated therapy; antiglaucoma drops were stopped on the day of surgery and resumed postoperatively if target IOP was not reached.
Tonometry: Goldmann by an experienced operator; two readings averaged, a third taken and the median recorded if the two differed by more than 2 mmHg (Methods 2.1).
Both arms are standard angle procedures combined with phacoemulsification without an investigational agent, so both are control groups (protocol: two standard techniques compared).
Number of antiglaucoma medications is tabulated in Table 4 and baseline in Table 1 R11 (not extracted; schema 1.0.0 has no medication series).
Day conversions: 1 day = 0.0329 months, 14 days = 0.46 months (days/30.4375, 4 decimals).
